cells.tense: Right now, the practice is running and your hands are steady on it.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Name the part of your practice you keep propping up out of habit, and stop propping it. Let it go quiet and see whether it was ever needed.
cells.core:
There is a steadiness under your practice that does not need pushing. You show up, you repeat the thing, it gets better in small increments. The work itself is calm, and the solitude is where it feeds you rather than where it hides you.

Not everything you carry is load-bearing. Name the part of your practice you keep propping up out of habit, and stop propping it. Let it go quiet and see whether it was ever needed. What was false falls quickly and quietly, and there is less to brace against than you expected. What is left stands without help, and the practice gets lighter to keep.
cells.sheetLine: The practice holds you back, and it holds you up.
cells.verb: Keeping a practice alive through repetition — the small daily return to a craft
cells.place: Where you hold steady under load and keep going — the place endurance lives

cells.tense: By the time you look up, the practice will have closed the door behind you.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Pick what you have been polishing longest and set it down, unfinished, for two days. Keep your hands off it till the second night.
cells.core:
The practice has tightened into something brittle. The hours grow, the standards sharpen, and stopping has started to feel like losing ground. You are holding the shape so hard it takes effort to breathe inside it.

Pick what you have been polishing longest and set it down, unfinished, for two days. Keep your hands off it till the second night. The grip is not the work. What you make well on Tuesday is still there Thursday, and the gap shows you something you cannot see with your hands on it. Nothing is gained by holding on the whole time, and nothing is lost when you don't.

cells.tense: Years back, something made picking up the practice again feel like a risk you stopped taking.
cells.act: put it in proportion, not in punishment
cells.ask: Do one small stretch of the thing you stopped, then stop there — no catching up, no making it count for anything.
cells.core:
The practice has gone quiet, and it stays that way. You do not keep at anything long enough for it to build, and the longer that goes on, the stranger the first stretch feels. The ability is still in you. It just has not been asked to do anything yet.

Do one small stretch of the thing you stopped, then stop there — no catching up, no making it count for anything. A practice that owes no debt is easier to pick up than one that has been tallying what you missed. One return, kept light, tells you what it costs and what it gives. Decide from there, or don't decide at all.

cells.tense: You keep a practice going right now and would not call it that if asked.
cells.act: move through the fog without demanding the map
cells.ask: Take the thing you are already good at and do it once more slowly, no plan for where it leads. Stop when it stops being easy.
cells.core:
You have a practice that runs whether or not you attend to it. It shows in how good you have gotten at something you do not count, and you would likely say you are not the kind who practices at all. The work happens anyway. That is the part worth keeping.

Take the thing you are already good at and do it once more slowly, no plan for where it leads. Stop when it stops being easy. You do not need to see the whole road to take it; one step is enough light to know how the step feels. You built this by repetition, and doing it on purpose once puts it back where you can find it.
cells.sheetLine: You already practice — you just don't call it that.
